dismissedFlows.title: Run the service
dismissedFlows.note: A startup tour bundling configuration defaults, boot migrations, the startup log line and the health probe into one test. The health behaviour is asserted by check-service-health and the configuration defaults by print-configuration-with-a-redacted-database-password.

dismissedFlows.title: Keep a member token working after restart
dismissedFlows.note: Asserting this needs the service restarted midway through a single scenario, which the api driver cannot express — a scenario boots one server. The statelessness it rests on is a property of the token, not an endpoint response.

dismissedFlows.title: Start bookclub and manage a first book
dismissedFlows.note: The re-synthesized whole-product tour: every milestone it walks is already asserted by a focused flow (check-service-health, print-configuration, the member-token refusals, the duplicate-ISBN refusal); bundling them adds no coverage and no single scenario expresses them faithfully — the same verdict recorded for its predecessor start-the-bookclub-service-and-manage-a-book-on-the-shelf.

dismissedFlows.title: Add, list, retrieve, and finish a book
dismissedFlows.note: A multi-operation tour across sections, duplicating flows that already pass one behaviour at a time; a scenario is bound to one operation, so its response-schema assertions cannot span the tour. Same verdict as its predecessor add-find-view-cover-and-finish-a-book.

dismissedFlows.title: Finish a book and re-stamp it
dismissedFlows.note: Re-stamping can only be shown by comparing two finishedAt timestamps across steps, which the expectation vocabulary cannot state. The finish behaviour itself is asserted by require-member-token-to-finish-a-book and handle-finishing-an-unknown-book. Same verdict as its predecessor finish-and-re-finish-a-book.

dismissedFlows.title: Add a book and prevent duplicate ISBNs
dismissedFlows.note: Bundles ISBN normalisation with the one-copy-per-ISBN refusal; the fidelity reviewer rejects every authored form of the pair. Both halves already pass on their own — reject-an-invalid-isbn covers normalisation and add-a-duplicate-isbn covers the 409. Same verdict as its predecessor add-a-book-and-prevent-another-copy-of-the-same-isbn.

dismissedFlows.title: Reject unauthenticated member changes
dismissedFlows.note: States the token refusal across BOTH member operations, and a scenario bound to one operation cannot carry schema assertions for the other. Each operation's refusal is asserted on its own by require-member-token-to-add-a-book and require-member-token-to-finish-a-book.

dismissedFlows.title: Adding a book that is already on the shelf returns a duplicate conflict
dismissedFlows.note: Duplicates add-a-duplicate-isbn behaviour-for-behaviour (same 201-then-409 pair on POST /books), and both insert the newBookRequest fixture — on a shared board run whichever dispatches second meets 409 on its FIRST insert and reads as drift. Birth validates each in isolation, so the collision only shows on the board. One flow carries the conflict claim; this one adds no coverage.
